anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have their separate ground pins tied to the same board ground net: U1 pins 4 and 5 (GND1/GND2) and U49 pins 4 and 5 (GND1/GND2) are all on GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes two isolated CAN buses implemented through isolated CAN transceivers; an isolated transceiver requires its controller-side and bus-side ground domains to remain separate (or otherwise be isolated) for the isolation to work.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`) ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The CAN transceivers are not galvanically isolated from the logic side, so the intended isolated CAN-bus behavior is defeated and ground loops or loss of isolation protection can occur.

anomalies.observed: The common anode net for the Ethernet status LEDs, /NET0185, contains only D17 pin 2, D43 pin 2, and D49 pin 2; it is not connected to +3V3 or any other supply.
anomalies.expected: For these LEDs to light, their common anodes should be tied to the appropriate positive supply (normally +3V3 for the CM4 Ethernet LED outputs), with cathodes driven through the current-limiting resistors.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet status LEDs cannot light because their anodes are floating/unpowered.

anomalies.observed: One half of the dual LED D46 has both of its terminals connected to the same net: D46 pin 4 (A2) is directly on NET0012, and D46 pin 2 (K2) is connected through R54 to NET0012.
anomalies.expected: An LED indicator should have its anode and cathode connected across two different potentials (for example, anode to the driven signal and cathode to ground through a current-limiting resistor, or vice versa), not both terminals to the same net.
anomalies.impact: The second LED element of D46 is effectively shorted through R54 and will not illuminate.

parsed.summary: The design files support at least one real deviation: the isolated CAN transceivers have their separate ground domains tied together, defeating the specified isolated CAN-bus architecture. The files also show an unpowered Ethernet LED common-anode net and one dual-LED element wired with both terminals on the same net.

In netlist, U46 pin6 SENSE to +5V. U46 pin1 VIN to NET0002 (USB-C VBUS). U46 pin5 GATE to Q13 gate. Q13 source to +5V, drain to NET0002. Thus VIN should be input (source side?), SENSE output (load side). For P-FET, source should be VIN side, drain SENSE side. If input is USB-C VBUS and output is +5V, then Q13 source should be VBUS, drain +5V, U46 VIN VBUS, SENSE +5V. But netlist has Q13 source +5V, drain VBUS, U46 VIN VBUS, SENSE +5V.
